why: An agent orienting itself before reading. The container mounts corpus read-only at /app/corpus and the server is launched with that as its only allowed root, so every path here sits inside it.

First of four reads that share the 21-byte prefix /app/corpus/context/. With structured file arguments the shared material is the directory, and that is not an artefact of this corpus: agents read several files from one directory at once.
Sibling read. Differs from the previous call in the last nine bytes of the path.
Third sibling, and the file carrying planted bait tokens, so a local control that egresses would be egressing something recognisable.

The bait file, bounded to its last twenty lines. Pulls the planted tokens into the MCP response, which is the 'what came back into context' axis: for a local control it makes the negative meaningful, since the bait is in hand and still nothing leaves.

One call reading two files, which is where a per-call fan-out figure would show a server opening more than one thing per invocation. Its argument set contains both paths, so it competes with any other call naming either of them.
Metadata-only read of a file the previous call also names, so two concurrent calls genuinely share a fragment without either being a copy of the other.
A glob search, the one call here whose argument is a pattern rather than a path. Cheap on a directory this small.
A recursive listing, bounded by the directory being small. Exercises a third code path at a path that shares only /app/corpus/ with the reads above.

The argument-less call. It contributes no digests at all, so under concurrency it is a candidate that can never win a content match: the wave therefore contains one call whose only possible grade comes from the window.
